title: Naringin promotes hair regeneration via wnt/beta-catenin pathway: A dose-dependent study in C57BL/6J mice.
authors: Zheng, XianPing; Hu, JingLu; Chen, ZiLiang; Liao, MingDe; Luo, ShuLin; Lu, SiDing; Lin, BoJie
one_liner_zh: 该文研究柚皮苷通过Wnt/β-catenin通路促进小鼠毛发再生，仅涉及小分子-蛋白对接，无蛋白质-DNA互作体系，与本课题无关。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Alopecia, especially androgenetic alopecia (AGA), is a common condition affecting many individuals globally, impacting both men and women. Current treatments, such as minoxidil and finasteride, have limitations regarding efficacy and side effects. Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) offers alternative treatments, with naringin-a flavonoid found in Citrus species-emerging as a potential candidate due to its influence on the Wnt/beta-catenin signaling pathway, a key regulator of hair follicle growth. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This study assessed the effects of naringin on hair regeneration in C57BL/6J mice through a dose-dependent approach. Mice were divided into five groups (1 %, 2 %, 4 % naringin, saline, and 5 % minoxidil). Hair regrowth was evaluated via macroscopic and histological examinations, immunohistochemistry, and molecular biology assays. Expression levels of key proteins in the Wnt/beta-catenin pathway were measured, and molecular docking was performed to investigate interactions between naringin and beta-catenin. RESULTS: The 4 % naringin group exhibited superior hair growth, with significantly higher hair follicle density and greater cell proliferation compared to other groups, including the 5 % minoxidil group. Molecular analysis confirmed enhanced expression of Wnt10b, beta-catenin, and VEGF-A, along with a reduction in Wnt5a. Molecular docking revealed stable binding between naringin and beta-catenin, suggesting a specific interaction that may mediate its effects. CONCLUSIONS: Naringin promotes hair regeneration through activation of the Wnt/beta-catenin signaling pathway, with the 4 % concentration showing the best results. This natural compound, particularly at 4 % concentration, demonstrates hair growth-promoting efficacy comparable to 5 % minoxidil by activating the Wnt/beta-catenin pathway, offering a promising alternative for alopecia treatment.
abstract_zh: 背景：脱发，尤其是雄激素性脱发（androgenetic alicata, AGA），是一种影响全球许多个体的常见疾病，波及男性和女性。当前治疗方法，如米诺地尔（minoxidil）和非那雄胺（finasteride），在疗效和副作用方面存在局限性。传统中医（Traditional Chinese Medicine, TCM）提供了替代疗法，其中柚皮苷（naringin）——一种存在于柑橘属（Citrus）物种中的黄酮类化合物——因其对Wnt/β-catenin信号通路（毛囊生长的关键调控因子）的影响，而成为潜在候选药物。材料与方法：本研究通过剂量依赖性方法，评估了柚皮苷对C57BL/6J小鼠毛发再生的影响。小鼠被分为五组（1%、2%、4%柚皮苷、生理盐水，以及5%米诺地尔）。通过宏观和组织学检查、免疫组织化学以及分子生物学检测评估毛发再生情况。测量了Wnt/β-catenin通路中关键蛋白的表达水平，并进行分子对接（molecular docking）以研究柚皮苷与β-catenin之间的相互作用。结果：4%柚皮苷组表现出优异的毛发生长，与其他组（包括5%米诺地尔组）相比，毛囊密度显著更高，细胞增殖更明显。分子分析确认Wnt10b、β-catenin和VEGF-A表达增强，同时Wnt5a表达减少。分子对接显示柚皮苷与β-catenin之间具有稳定结合，提示可能存在介导其效应的特异性相互作用。结论：柚皮苷通过激活Wnt/β-catenin信号通路促进毛发再生，其中4%浓度效果最佳。这种天然化合物，尤其在4%浓度下，通过激活Wnt/β-catenin通路，展现出与5%米诺地尔相当的促毛发生长功效，为脱发治疗提供了一种有前景的替代选择。
